newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian central bank says to ease monetary reins.
newsitem.headline: Croatian central bank says to ease monetary reins.

text.p: Croatia's central bank said on Wednesday it would ease tight monetary reins in April by trimming reserve requirement by one percentage point to 34.85 percent to meet stronger seasonal demand for money.
The decision follows March cuts of the discount and Lombard rates to 5.9 and 9.5 percent, respectively, after months of rigidity as the bank kept a watchful eye on overall stability.
"Demand usually increases in the Easter month and it just happens to come a bit earlier this year," executive director for research and analysis Velimir Sonje told Reuters.
"We think this is no short-term phenomenon. It could last until autumn," he said.
The reserve requirement cut is likely to release around 100 million kuna into the banking sector, Sonje said.

But the bank saw no threat in this to prices or the kuna exchange rate after warning against possible inflationary movements earlier this year, as commercial banks were thought to be better at sterilising their temporary surpluses.

More kuna in circulation is also aimed to counter the effect that larger seasonal currency inflows, partly due to tourism earnings, usually have on the nominal appreciation of the kuna in this period, Sonje said.
"We do not want the exchange rate to strengthen and prices obviously cannot fall," he added.
February retail prices were flat after a 1.0 percent monthly rise in January. Year-on-year, inflation ran at 3.7 percent last month.
The kuna is now quoted at around 6.0 to the dollar and 3.57 to the German mark, hardly changed from the levels it was introduced at in May 1994. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
